blocks.text: Half-day tour (4 h) to Corcovado with an English-speaking guide: an open eco-train climbs through the Tijuca Forest to the 38-metre statue of Christ the Redeemer, at 710 m, completed in 1931, with a breathtaking panorama of the Rio–Niterói Bridge, Guanabara Bay, the Botanical Garden, the Maracanã Stadium and Sugar Loaf. In the evening, watch the sunset from the Arpoador rocks.

provenance.rationale: Highlight heading labels the two included sides of Iguazu described in the Word programme.

blocks.text:
Tour of the Brazilian side of the falls with an English-speaking guide. Their name means “big water” in Guaraní: the falls thunder down up to about 80 metres into the Devil’s Throat gorge, in striking contrast to the calm river above.

Tour of the Argentine side with a guide. Across the Tancredo Neves Bridge, trails and walkways take you right up to the falls, where you feel the power of the water up close and see the Devil’s Throat, the largest of them all, with rainbows hanging over the cascades.
